notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Moving management groups and subscriptions” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: If the Owner role on the subscription is inherited from the current management group, your move targets are limited. You can move the subscription only to another management group where you have the Owner role. You can't move the subscription to a management group where you're only a Contributor because you would lose ownership of the subscription.

notes.front: You moved a management group, but the portal still shows the old hierarchy. How long can this last?
notes.back: Up to 30 minutes.
notes.explanation: Resource Manager caches the hierarchy details for that long, so the portal might not show the move at once.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Moving management groups and subscriptions” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Azure Resource Manager caches details of the management group hierarchy for up to 30 minutes. As a result, the Azure portal might not immediately show that you moved a management group.

notes.front: What is the root management group’s default display name, and what is its identifier?
notes.back: Tenant root group; its identifier is the same value as the Microsoft Entra tenant’s.
notes.explanation: Although it is built in, it works as a management group in its own right, at the top of the hierarchy.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Important facts about the root management group” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: By default, the root management group's display name is **Tenant root group**, and it operates itself as a management group. The ID is the same value as the Microsoft Entra tenant ID.

notes.front: Can the root management group be moved or deleted?
notes.back: No, unlike other management groups.
notes.explanation: All subscriptions and management groups in the directory fold up into it.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Important facts about the root management group” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: - The root management group can't be moved or deleted, unlike other management groups. - All subscriptions and management groups fold up into one root management group within the directory.

notes.front: Where do new subscriptions land in the management group hierarchy when they are created?
notes.back: In the root management group, by default.
notes.explanation: All resources in the directory fold up to the root management group for global management.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Important facts about the root management group” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: - All resources in the directory fold up to the root management group for global management. - New subscriptions automatically default to the root management group when they're created.

notes.front: Who has default access to the root management group, and who can elevate to gain it?
notes.back: No one by default; only Microsoft Entra Global Administrators can elevate themselves.
notes.explanation: Once they have access, they can assign any Azure role to other users to manage the group.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Important facts about the root management group” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: No one has default access to the root management group. Microsoft Entra Global Administrators are the only users who can elevate themselves to gain access. After they have access to the root management group, they can assign any Azure role to other users to manage the group.

notes.front: An engineer proposes assigning a convenient but optional policy on the root management group. What does Microsoft advise?
notes.back: Keep user access and policy assignments at the root to “must have” items only.
notes.explanation: Anything assigned there applies to all resources in the directory.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Important facts about the root management group” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Any assignment of user access or policy on the root management group applies to all resources within the directory. Because of this access level, all customers should evaluate the need to have items defined on this scope. User access and policy assignments should be "must have" only at this scope.

notes.front: What must all subscriptions within a single management group trust?
notes.back: The same Microsoft Entra tenant.
notes.explanation: Management groups give enterprise-grade management at scale whatever type of subscriptions you have.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Management groups give you enterprise-grade management at scale, no matter what type of subscriptions you might have. However, all subscriptions within a single management group must trust the same Microsoft Entra tenant.

notes.front: You assign an Azure role at a management group. Where does it take effect?
notes.back: It inherits down the hierarchy to the child resources beneath the management group.
notes.explanation: Management groups support Azure role-based access control for all resource access and role definitions.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Management group access” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Azure management groups support Azure RBAC for all resource access and role definitions. Child resources that exist in the hierarchy inherit these permissions. Any Azure role can be assigned to a management group that inherits down the hierarchy to the resources.

notes.front: Twelve subscriptions need the same access for an audit team. What is the simplest approach using management groups?
notes.back: Place the subscriptions under one management group and create a single role assignment on it.
notes.explanation: One assignment on the management group saves scripting role-based access control across each subscription.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What are Azure management groups?”, “Hierarchy of management groups and subscriptions” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: By moving multiple subscriptions under a management group, you can create one Azure role assignment on the management group. The role inherits that access to all the subscriptions. One assignment on the management group can enable users to have access to everything they need, instead of scripting Azure role-based access control (RBAC) over different subscriptions.
